brief:
Jeremy Konyndyk, president of Refugees International, dismissed Israeli government claims about improved malnutrition figures in Gaza as "absurd on its face," according to Middle East Eye. Konyndyk contended that better nutrition statistics do not invalidate earlier findings of famine conditions across the territory, challenging the Israeli narrative on food security.

The disagreement reflects a broader divide between humanitarian organizations operating in Gaza and Israeli officials over the scale and severity of food insecurity. Israel has pointed to data suggesting nutritional improvements among the Palestinian population, while aid groups have maintained that malnutrition persists despite any marginal gains. Konyndyk's statement underscores the ongoing dispute over whether conditions in Gaza meet the threshold of famine.
